title: Unit – 3 : Session – 4 : SLO – 1 | Thread Priority and Daemon Threads
sections: Fill: The default priority of a thread in Java is 5 (Thread.NORM_PRIORITY).
T/F: Daemon threads continue running even after all user threads have finished. — FALSE (the JVM exits when only daemon threads remain)
MCQ: Method used to set the priority → C) setPriority()
Fill: The priority range for threads in Java is from 1 to 10.
Find the output: setDaemon(true) before start(), print isDaemon() → A) true
T/F: Calling setDaemon(true) after start() will throw an exception. — TRUE (IllegalThreadStateException)
MCQ: Thread type used for background services like garbage collection → C) Daemon thread
Fill: The method ISDAEMON() returns whether a thread is a daemon.
Identify the error: setDaemon(true) after start() → C) IllegalThreadStateException
Fill: Threads with higher priority are MORE likely to be scheduled before lower priority threads.
